theory.heading: What Logging in Python is
theory.body: Logging in Python describes the methods and patterns used within Python Training Course to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Logging in Python is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Logging in Python matters
theory.body: Without Logging in Python, systems built with Python Training Course are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Logging in Python works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Logging in Python follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Logging in Python.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Logging in Python
theory.body: Logging in Python offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
